title: First-stage food processing: extraction rates for New Zealand

sources.citation: FAO Statistics Division. Technical Conversion Factors for Agricultural Commodities (undated; fao.org/fileadmin/templates/ess/documents/methodology/tcf.pdf), New Zealand, printed pages 694-697: crops and derived products, and milk.

items.description: Product obtained from milling or malting a New Zealand cereal, as a share of the grain processed
items.note: NEW ZEALAND, CROPS AND DERIVED PRODUCTS, Extraction rates %: Flour of Wheat 78, Bran of Wheat 22; Malt of Barley 80; Oats, Rolled 57, Bran of Oats 25. Wheat's two add to 100; oats' to 82, the rest being hulls and loss.

items.description: Dairy product obtained from New Zealand whole cow milk, as a share of the milk processed into that product
items.note: MILK, Extraction rates %: Cream, Fresh 11; Butter of Cow Milk 6.1; Whole Milk, Condensed 20; Whole Milk, Evaporated 45; Dry Whole Cow Milk 14; Cheese (Whole Cow Milk) 9. Each is a separate use of the milk, not shares of one stream. The same page gives 3,000 kg a milking animal, older than FAOSTAT's 4,593 kg (2023) used by the farm.
